title: EIDD-3525 is a broad-spectrum antiviral against alphavirus infection that targets the nsP4 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
abstract: Mosquito-transmitted alphaviruses, including chikungunya (CHIKV), Mayaro, Eastern equine encephalitis, and Venezuelan equine encephalitis viruses, cause severe arthritic or neurologic disease in humans. There are currently no approved antiviral treatments against alphavirus infection. Here, we report that the purine ribonucleoside EIDD-3525 is a potent inhibitor of alphavirus replication in vitro with broad spectrum antiviral activity against the Alphavirus genus. Using a trans-replicase assay, we find that EIDD-3525 blocks alphavirus RNA replication. Mutational profiling suggests that EIDD-3525 targets the alphavirus nsP4 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase that is conserved across medically important alphaviruses. In a pre-clinical mouse model of CHIKV infection and disease, oral treatment with EIDD-3525 reduced viral tissue burdens and the severity of virus-induced disease. Collectively, our findings support the continued development of the purine ribonucleoside EIDD-3525 as an orally available antiviral therapeutic for use against a broad group of alphaviruses.

title: Evaluation of Machine Learning Models for Predicting Breeding Values of Key Performance Traits in Iranian Crossbred (Thoroughbred × Turkmen) Racehorses.
abstract: Accurate prediction of breeding values (BVs) is fundamental to genetic improvement in racehorses. Although single-trait mixed models (STM), typically implemented using BLUP-based procedures, remain the standard framework for genetic evaluation, machine learning (ML) methods offer a flexible, data-driven approach for learning complex relationships among phenotypic, environmental, and pedigree-derived information. These capabilities have encouraged researchers to explore the application of ML methods for predicting breeding values. This study compared the performance of 13 ML algorithms for predicting estimated breeding values (EBVs) of Race Completion Time (RCT), Rank at the End of Competition (REC), and Average Speed (AS) in Iranian crossbred racehorses. A total of 55,070 race records from 5,296 horses were analyzed. Reference EBVs were estimated using single-trait mixed models (STM) fitted by maximum likelihood in Wombat. Thirteen ML algorithms, including linear regression models, tree-based ensembles, boosting methods, and artificial neural networks (ANNs), were trained using 75% of the data and evaluated on the remaining 25%. Predictive performance was assessed using accuracy, correlation, mean absolute error (MAE), mean squared error (MSE), bias, and dispersion. All ML models outperformed the conventional STM across the three traits. ANN consistently achieved the highest predictive performance, with accuracies of 0.63, 0.72, and 0.56 and correlations of 75%, 86%, and 71% for RCT, REC, and AS, respectively. XGBoost, LightGBM, Gradient Boosting and Random Forest also showed strong predictive ability, whereas linear models and distance-based methods exhibited comparatively lower performance. Prediction bias remained close to zero, and dispersion coefficients were generally close to unity across ML models. Machine learning, particularly ANN and boosting-based algorithms, substantially improved EBV prediction compared with the conventional STM. These findings demonstrate the potential of ML as a complementary tool for accelerating routine genetic evaluation and supporting more reliable selection decisions in horse breeding programs.

title: Medical Therapies for the Treatment of Osteoarthritis in the Horse - 20 years later….
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a debilitating joint disease, characterized by a degenerative catabolic cascade resulting in detrimental changes to all aspects of the joint including the irreversible destruction of articular cartilage. In 2006, a narrative review by Goodrich and Nixon outlined the available treatments for the medical management of OA; however, since that time substantial progress has been made. In recent years the therapeutic options for veterinarians managing horses with OA has increased significantly with a multitude of products available on the market. While many of the conventional treatments remain in clinical use, ongoing research continues to refine their application and evaluate their efficacy. Since their introduction, orthobiologic therapeutics have undergone extensive development, resulting in the emergence of numerous allogenic and autologous therapeutics. Similarly, cellular based therapies have advanced considerably. Overall, these advancements reflect a broader shift in treatment from those aimed predominantly at symptom management to interventions designed to modify the OA disease process. This narrative review follows up on the past 20 years of progress, outlining current evidence-based recommendations to provide a comprehensive guide for clinicians selecting therapeutic agents to treat horses with OA.

title: Equine-Assisted Learning and Social-Emotional Competence in Higher Education: An Exploratory Study of Emerging Adults' Experiences.
journal: The Journal of adolescent health : official publication of the Society for Adolescent Medicine
abstract: Equine-assisted learning (EAL) is an experiential educational approach that engages learners in structured human-horse activities to support character development, interpersonal growth, and life skills. Social-emotional learning (SEL) is increasingly recognized as an important aspect of student development, supporting both wellbeing and academic success. Although much studies have explored how horses may support human health and wellbeing, limited research has explored how undergraduate students experience EAL in relation to SEL within non-Western higher education contexts. An exploratory study was conducted to examine undergraduate students' experiences of participating in an 8-week EAL program at a private Malaysian institution. Fifteen participants (ages 18-24; 73.3% male, 26.7% female) engaged in structured experiential sessions involving guided human-horse interactions. In-depth, semistructured interviews were conducted. The qualitative data were analyzed using an inductive reflexive thematic analysis. Three themes were identified: (1) emotional learning through human-horse interactions, (2) interpersonal engagement through shared activities, and (3) transfer and application of learning. This study suggests that EAL may support SEL processes in higher education, while highlighting the need for further research to examine its effectiveness across diverse settings.

title: Pulled-up race outcomes as welfare-relevant surveillance indicators in United States Steeplechase horses, 2023-2025.
abstract: Pulled-up race outcomes are routinely recorded but are nonspecific, potentially reflecting fatigue, poor performance, footing, rider judgment, suspected injury, or physiological compromise. We evaluated their association with subsequent participation disruption in United States steeplechase horses. National Steeplechase Association Race Results Reports from 2023 to 2025 were analyzed retrospectively at the horse-start level. Outcomes were time to the next later-date start, ≥60-day interruption, ≥183-day absence, and no recorded later-date start. Cox models were stratified by race type with horse-clustered robust covariance; binary outcomes used horse-clustered generalized estimating equations. Sensitivity analyses excluded November starts because racing is seasonal from March through November. Among 3,070 starts by 710 horses, 367 (11.95%) were pulled up, involving 277 horses (39.0%). No later-date start was recorded after 37.6% of pulled-up and 21.2% of non-pulled-up starts. Among returners, median time to the next start was 42 versus 35 days; Kaplan-Meier medians for all starts were 148 versus 45 days. Pulled-up status was associated with a lower recorded return rate (hazard ratio 0.589, 95% confidence interval 0.515-0.675). Race-type-adjusted odds ratios were 2.10 (1.67-2.64) for ≥60-day interruption and 2.36 (1.80-3.10) for ≥183-day absence. Associations persisted after excluding November starts. Pulled-up outcomes were associated with participation disruption, although clinical reasons were unavailable. They may help prioritize follow-up and longitudinal surveillance but cannot replace veterinary examination or clinical records.

title: The Impact of Systemic Treatment With Flunixin Meglumine on the Two Antiproteases Alpha-2-Macroglobulin (A2M) and Alpha-1-Antitrypsin (A1AT) in Equine Plasma and Platelet-Rich Fibrin (PRF).
abstract: To evaluate the effect of flunixin meglumine, a systemic non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID), on the antiproteases, A2M and A1AT, in equine plasma and PRF. A prospective cross-sectional study. Plasma, solid PRF, and liquid PRF were collected from a control-group that included healthy horses not treated with NSAIDs within the last 3 months. The NSAID-group were ophthalmology patients with no systemic inflammatory disease, and all received a full dose of flunixin meglumine (1.1 mg/kg BID PO or IV) for three or more days prior to collection. Samples were collected and prepared using a standardized protocol for plasma and PRF preparation. Concentrations of A2M and A1AT were analyzed with ELISA kits. Statistical analysis with Mann-Whitney U tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests was performed using significance set at p 0.05). Plasma had a significantly higher amount of A2M compared to solid and liquid PRF (both p < 0.001). Solid PRF had the highest concentration of A1AT and was significantly higher when compared to liquid PRF (p < 0.001), but not when compared to plasma (p = 0.071). The systemic NSAID, flunixin meglumine, does not appear to significantly alter antiprotease concentrations in equine plasma or PRF. Although PRF should not be used as a replacement for plasma, solid PRF may be a good adjunctive therapy for the treatment of keratomalacia due to its high A1AT concentration.

title: Global prevalence of equine piroplasmosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis of evidence from 2020-2025.
abstract: Equine piroplasmosis remains a major constraint to equine health, productivity, and international movement. In compliance with PRISMA 2020 criteria, a systematic review and meta-analysis were carried out to estimate the pooled global prevalence of equine piroplasmosis and identify possible sources of risk variables. Databases including PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Springer Nature, Europe PMC, Cochrane Library, ProQuest, CABI Digital Library, and Google Scholar were searched between 2020 to 2025. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to calculate pooled prevalence estimates. Subgroup analyses, meta-regression, and publication bias assessments were conducted using RStudio software version 4.6.0. Among the 95 studies included in the analysis, the pooled prevalence of active T. equi infection was 25.21%, while the corresponding seroprevalence was 30.96%. For active B. caballi infection, the pooled prevalence was 4.60%, compared with a seroprevalence of 10.90%. The pooled prevalence of active T. haneyi infection was 12.18%. Substantial heterogeneity (I² > 90%) was identified across all pooled estimates, likely reflecting differences in sampling periods and sample sizes, geographic regions, diagnostic approaches, and host demographics. Meta-regression revealed a significant increasing temporal trend in T. equi prevalence (p 0.05). Equine piroplasmosis remains highly prevalent worldwide, particularly T. equi, with marked heterogeneity driven by methodological factors, geographic region, and host characteristics. These findings underscore the need for standardized surveillance, harmonized diagnostics, and integrated vector control strategies to mitigate the global impact of equine piroplasmosis.

title: Cryo-EM reveals a C15 annular stacking assembly of the VEEV nsP3 Alphavirus Unique Domain.
abstract: Alphaviruses are arthropod-borne pathogens that cause significant human disease, including severe arthritis and encephalitis. Among the four nonstructural proteins (nsP1-nsP4) that form the viral replication complex (RC), nsP3 is the least functionally characterized. Recent studies have shown that CHIKV-nsP3 forms a right-handed helical scaffold, while Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV) nsP3 forms gel-like biomolecular condensates mediated by its Alphavirus Unique Domain (AUD). In this study, we used cryo-electron microscopy to reveal a closed annular stacking assembly of VEEV-nsP3, composed of C15-symmetric rings that stack axially without helical offset-fundamentally differing from the helical arrangement of CHIKV. Structural comparisons demonstrate that this divergence arises from the loss of three key hydrogen bond networks, particularly an axial hydrogen bond that drives helical propagation in CHIKV but is uniquely absent in VEEV. Furthermore, we propose that the proteolytic cleavage at the nsP2/nsP3 junction regulates the annular to tubular transition. Our work provides insights into the structural diversity and dynamic regulation of alphavirus RC crown formation, with implications for understanding replication complex assembly across this viral lineage.

title: The RLR-MAVS-IRF3 axis activates the IFN pathway to restrict Tonate virus (TONV) infection.
abstract: Tonate virus (TONV) is a neglected mosquito-borne alphavirus of the Venezuelan equine encephalitis complex associated with febrile illness, encephalitis, and fetal central nervous system abnormalities. Yet, host pathways that sense TONV infection and restrict its replication remain poorly defined. Here, we investigated the interaction between TONV and the type I interferon (IFN-I) system in human T98G and A549 cells. We show that TONV infection led to the accumulation of cytosolic double-stranded RNA and a robust IFN response. RIG-I and MDA5 depletion as well as that of MAVS and IRF3 strongly reduced TONV-induced IFN response. Disruption of RIG-I, MDA5, MAVS, or IRF3 resulted in an increase of dsRNA-positive cells and a higher viral RNA accumulation. Finally, we found that treatment with exogenous IFN-I strongly inhibits TONV replication reducing both viral RNA loads and infectious particle production. Thus, together, our results identify the RIG-I/MDA5-MAVS-IRF3 axis as a major pathway sensing TONV infection and establishing an IFN-I-dependent antiviral state, providing the first molecular characterization of TONV innate immune sensing in human cells.

title: New Noninvasive Long-Term Stress indicator in Horses: Analysis of Cortisol Levels in the Hoof of Foals.
journal: Animal science journal = Nihon chikusan Gakkaiho
abstract: Noninvasive sampling methods are recommended in animals as far as possible. However, there has been no way to safely measure long-term stress in all horses including foals and stallions. Currently, nail cortisol in humans has been reported to be a promising noninvasive long-term stress indicator. This study aimed to evaluate the usefulness of a horse's hoof as a noninvasive long-term stress indicator by determining whether hoof cortisol levels varied similarly to hair cortisol levels noted in a previous study. All hooves were sampled by one farrier after a foal's birth. They were divided into three groups: (1) hooves reflecting cortisol levels 1 month prior to birth of fetuses (n = 18), (2) the 1 month-period immediately after birth (n = 11), and (3) the 1 month-period more than 1 month after birth (n = 9). Cortisol levels in the fetal period markedly exceeded those of the other two periods (p < 0.05). Moreover, the changes of cortisol levels in this study were consistent with those of similar periods in previous studies. Therefore, the hoof would be useful to obtain noninvasive long-term stress indicators in the horse.

title: Is promoting health equity through a well-being economy a Trojan horse for a post-capitalist socialist economy? Will it make it through the public policy gates?
abstract: BackgroundAttempts to promote health equity through traditional means of public policy advocacy have proven profoundly unsuccessful in Canada. Despite decades of research, policy statements and declarations as to the importance of addressing the causes of health inequalities that prematurely sicken and kill, the quality and equitable distribution of the living and working conditions, i.e., the social determinants of health, continue to decline.PurposeIn this paper we examine the most recent attempt to promote public policy to reverse these developments - the well-being economy - that calls for "an economy designed to serve people and the planet, not the other way around" which has similarities with the coexisting concept of a post-capitalist socialist economy.AnalysisWe compare and contrast the assumptions of both approaches through a critical materialist political economy perspective lens and their likelihood of moving the health equity-promoting public policy agenda forward.FindingsWe found most of the well-being economy literature's preferred outcomes are remarkably consistent with the vision of a post-capitalist socialist economy that puts the well-being of people above profit-making. However, the means by which advocates propose these outcomes may come about are profoundly different. The omission of the terms socialist or socialism in the well-being economy literature suggests its advocates may see it as a Trojan Horse for infiltrating these concepts into public policy discourse.ConclusionWe see the well-being economy concept as another well-meaning initiative to promote health equity that is likely to be ignored by governing authorities whose interests are aligned with those for whom such an economy would conflict with their profit-making motives. Instead, we call for explicit consideration of a post-capitalist socialist economy and how it could move us towards a health equity promoting society.

title: Revealing potential Atlantic salmon bycatch hotspots from pelagic fisheries landings across the Northeast Atlantic.
abstract: Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) marine survival has declined markedly over the past five decades, leading to concerns about future population viability. While many studies have explored the impacts of stressors such as climate change and predation, less is known about bycatch from pelagic fisheries targeting finfish species. This study, focused on the first few months of the salmon marine migration period, narrows down the space-time domains where pelagic fisheries bycatch is most likely to occur. Landings from an International Council for the Exploration of the Sea-led data call were used to assess bycatch exposure. Temporal patterns of monthly landings of six commercially important pelagic finfish species (mackerel Scomber scombrus, herring Clupea harengus, horse mackerel Trachurus trachurus, sardine Sardina pilchardus, capelin Mallotus villosus, and chub mackerel Scomber colias) within the Northeast Atlantic region from 2000 to 2022 were considered alongside reconstructed salmon migration regions. This study indicated that bycatch exposure from herring and mackerel fisheries was higher than that of other pelagic fisheries along the shared salmon migration corridor between April and August, with cumulative exposure highest over time for the herring fishery. Southern salmon populations were also exposed to the horse mackerel and sardine fisheries in April. Temporal patterns of monthly pelagic landings were compared with patterns of marine return rates in salmon index populations, but no consistent relationships were present. Quantifying salmon bycatch rates at sea remains challenging due to highly variable and sparse data but, given the severity of declines across their range, conservation measures that address factors affecting marine survival of salmon are urgently needed. Future investigations using emerging technology in the pelagic fisheries identified in this study could provide opportunities to develop more robust information on bycatch risk to Atlantic salmon stocks and to direct appropriate mitigation measures.

title: Clinical Efficacy of Varying Dosages of Intravenous Phenylbutazone in a Reversible Model of Equine Foot Lameness.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: The objective of this experiment was to compare the clinical efficacy of various dosages of phenylbutazone (PBZ) with a negative control. The hypothesis was that higher PBZ doses would result in improved efficacy in a dose-dependent manner. Eight horses were shod with adjustable heart bar shoes on one front foot. Grade 4.0/5.0 lameness was induced every 2 to 4 weeks by tightening a set screw against the heart bar. Heart rate (HR) and lameness score (LS) were monitored at rest; every 20 min after lameness induction for 5 h; and hourly for another 8 h. One hour after lameness induction, treatment was administered IV in a randomized blinded manner and included negative control (isotonic saline: SAL) or PBZ at 2.2 (LOW), 4.4 (MOD), or 8.8 (HIGH) mg/kg body weight. Jugular blood samples were obtained at experiment hours 0, 1:05, 3, 5, 9, and 13, and were evaluated for plasma PBZ concentration. Results were compared using repeated measures analysis of variance and Student-Newman-Keul's test with the level of significance set at p < 0.05. MOD and HIGH dose PBZ reduced HR from 3.0 h through 12.0 h and LS from 1.67 h through 12.0 h post-administration (p < 0.05); there was no difference in response between MOD and HIGH dose PBZ. Compared to SAL, LOW dose PBZ reduced HR from 3.67 h through 5.0 h and LS from 3.67 h through 4.0 h after administration (p < 0.05). The conclusions were that LOW dose PBZ was clinically effective for only a brief period compared to SAL, and HIGH dose was not more effective than MOD dose PBZ.

title: Proof of Concept for Open Flow Microperfusion for Intratumoural Drug Administration in Equine Cutaneous Neoplasia.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Intratumoural drug delivery can achieve high local therapeutic exposure while limiting systemic effects, but heterogeneous distribution may compromise treatment efficacy and precision. This proof-of-concept study investigated open flow microperfusion (OFM) as a novel platform for local delivery of tigilanol tiglate (TT), an intratumoural antineoplastic agent with immunomodulatory and vascular-disrupting effects. Four horses with histologically confirmed cutaneous neoplasia (three sarcoids and one squamous cell carcinoma) underwent OFM using TT concentrations of 0.01-0.04 mg/mL delivered at 9 µL/min for 7-24 h over one to three consecutive days. OFM systems were well tolerated and remained functional for up to three days. Localized vascular disruption, polymorphonuclear cell recruitment, oncosis and tissue sloughing developed in association with perfused regions, consistent with recognized TT-induced tissue responses. Two sarcoids exhibited biologic responses that did not result in complete local tumour ablation. Tumour ablation was achieved initially in one squamous cell carcinoma, although deep-seated disease subsequently progressed, while one sarcoid was ablated and remained tumour-free 497 days after treatment. These preliminary findings demonstrate that OFM allows precise, sustained intratumoural TT challenge, resulting in characteristic tissue responses supporting further investigation of this local delivery platform for tumour-targeted therapies.

title: Measuring the Rider-Horse Dyad Across Olympic Equestrian Disciplines: A Scoping Review of Methodological Gaps and Priorities for Show Jumping.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: (1) Background: Rider-horse coordination underpins equestrian performance; yet, its definition, quantitative indicators, and measurement methods remain inconsistent across Olympic disciplines. This scoping review mapped the constructs, metrics, and measurement approaches in dressage, show jumping, eventing, and transferable equestrian contexts, with show jumping as the principal application context. (2) Methods: Following PRISMA-ScR guidance and a Population-Concept-Context framework, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and PubMed were searched from database inception to 10 September 2026. Evidence was charted by discipline, measurement domain, measurement configuration, and synchronisation status. (3) Results: A total of 121 evidence sources were included. Among 108 empirical or methodological studies, 47 were kinematic/biomechanical, 23 performance/statistical, 15 behavioural/welfare-related, 13 kinetic/pressure/interface, and 10 neuromuscular/physiological. Only 12 used synchronised rider-horse time-series or event-based measurements, and none of the show-jumping studies met the strict synchronisation criterion. Coordination was commonly inferred from single-partner signals, interface measures, or aggregate performance outcomes. (4) Conclusions: The key limitation is not sensor availability, but the lack of validated dyadic methods. Future show-jumping studies should use common time bases, predefined biomechanical events, paired variables, and prospective validation, while integrating behavioural and clinical evidence when interpreting welfare-related outcomes.

title: Unveiling Equine Pathologies from an Iron Age Ritual Deposit: Health, Management and Biomechanical Stress in the Protohistoric Horses of Casas del Turuñuelo (Badajoz, Spain).
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Equids played a central economic and symbolic role in Iberian Iron Age society, yet little is known about their health and management during the protohistoric period. This study examines the unusually well-preserved equid assemblage from the Tartessian site of Casas del Turuñuelo (Badajoz, Spain), dating from the 5th century BCE with the aim of reconstructing patterns of pathology and biomechanical stress. Thirty-one individuals were subjected to macroscopic paleopathological assessment following established diagnostic criteria and, for a subset of seven individuals, computed tomography (CT) of the thoracic and lumbar vertebrae was performed. The results reveal a consistent combination of enamel hypoplasia, abnormal wear of the second premolars, and hyperostosis of the diastema, indicating episodes of systemic stress and chronic mechanical irritation, likely related to bitting or other handling practices. Thoracolumbar spondylosis deformans and enthesopathic changes in the limbs point to repetitive strain and axial overloading compatible with traction or intensive work. Occasional metapodial synostoses further support cumulative biomechanical stress in several individuals. Altogether, these findings suggest that the horses deposited in the ritual event had undergone prolonged and sometimes demanding use prior to death. The assemblage provides rare early evidence of equine workload, welfare conditions and husbandry strategies in the southwestern Iberian Protohistory.

title: Testicular Expression of Vitamin-D Receptor and Vitamin-D-Metabolizing Enzymes (CYP2R1, CYP27A1, and CYP27B1) in Normal and Cryptorchid Horses.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Vitamin D (VD) is required for testis activity being a key regulator of calcium and testosterone, both essential for spermatogenesis and sperm maturation. VD is activated by a metabolizing machinery of enzymes (CYP2R1, CYP27A1, CYP27B1) and acts throughout its receptor (VDR). Cryptorchidism is a developmental defect caused by the failed scrotal descend of the testicle and can compromise fertility depending on whether one or both testes are retained. Here, we reported the expression and localization of VDR- and VD-activating enzymes in the testis of normal and unilateral cryptorchid equines obtained by Real-Time PCR, Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. Results demonstrated that cryptorchidism affected gene and protein expression. Leydig cells expressed the highest level of VDR, CYP2R1, CYP27A1, and CYP27B1, whilst CYP27A1 and CYP27B1 were more abundant in spermatids from normal testes compared to scrotal testes of unilateral cryptorchid animals. No different cellular localization of the VD-metabolizing machinery was observed between cryptorchid and scrotal testicles, although some variation in staining intensity was observed. These results provide insights for further studies, required for clarifying VD's role in equine reproduction.

title: Oral Mosapride Attenuates Gastrointestinal Dysmotility During Experimental Endotoxemia in Horses: A Randomized, Blinded Crossover Study.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Endotoxemia is a major contributor to gastrointestinal hypomotility and postoperative ileus in horses. This study investigated whether oral mosapride retained prokinetic activity during acute lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced endotoxemia. Seven healthy adult horses were enrolled in a randomized, blinded, three-period crossover trial and received LPS alone, mosapride alone (MOSA), or LPS plus mosapride (LPS + MOSA), with a 14-day washout interval between periods. Mosapride was administered orally at 2 mg/kg, whereas endotoxemia was induced by an intravenous infusion of Escherichia coli O55:B5 LPS (0.03 µg/kg) over 30 min. Clinical variables, hematologic parameters, abdominal auscultation, and transabdominal ultrasonography were assessed from baseline to 6 h. LPS induced tachycardia, hyperthermia, leukocyte alterations, marked gastrointestinal hypomotility, gastric distension, and increased intestinal wall thickness. Mosapride alone increased gastrointestinal motility without clinically relevant abnormalities. During endotoxemia, mosapride partially restored gastrointestinal motility, reduced intestinal wall thickening and gastric distension, and was associated with a less pronounced hematologic inflammatory response than LPS alone. These findings indicate that oral mosapride retains clinically relevant prokinetic activity during acute experimental endotoxemia and support further investigation of its use as an adjunctive treatment for inflammation-associated gastrointestinal hypomotility in horses.

title: Proteomic Profiling and Targeted Validation Reveal a More Extensive Salivary than Serum Response to a Feed-Deprivation Protocol in Horses with Gastric Lesions.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Gastric ulceration is common in horses and remains challenging to diagnose, as gastroscopy is the gold standard. This study aimed to characterise the salivary and serum protein changes associated with a feed-deprivation protocol. Eight horses underwent this protocol, and gastric lesions were assessed by gastroscopy at the end of the experimental period. Saliva and blood samples were collected pre- and post-protocol, and pooled samples from each biological fluid and condition were analysed by two-dimensional gel electrophoresis to compare protein profiles. Fifteen salivary and five serum proteins showed differential abundance and were identified using mass spectrometry. Nine proteins were subsequently validated by Western blotting in individual samples, confirming the proteomic findings. The validated proteins are involved in multiple pathways, including inflammatory and immune responses (interleukins 1-F5 and -F6, prolactin-inducible protein, alpha-1-antitrypsin), metabolic and transport processes (albumin, serotransferrin, apolipoprotein A-IV, fatty acid-binding protein 5), and mucosal protection mechanisms (carbonic anhydrase VI, apolipoprotein A-IV, prolactin-inducible protein, fatty acid-binding protein 5). Compared with serum, saliva showed a more dynamic post-protocol proteomic response, with more proteins displaying altered abundance, supporting its versatility as a non-invasive matrix. Overall, these findings characterise salivary and serum responses associated with the feed-deprivation protocol in horses with gastric lesions confirmed post-protocol.

title: Retrospective Analysis of the Clinical Findings of 114 Horses with Eosinophilic Keratoconjunctivitis.
journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
abstract: Eosinophilic keratoconjunctivitis (EKC) is an inflammatory eye disease of horses with an unknown cause and suspected immune-mediated pathogenesis. This single-center retrospective case series included 114 horses (163 affected eyes) examined at a German equine referral hospital from January 2012 to December 2020. Of these horses, 71 (62.3%) were Warmbloods, 77 (67.5%) were presented from July to September, and 49 (43.0%) had bilateral disease. The cornea was involved in 139 of 163 eyes (85.3%). During the study period, 114 EKC cases occurred among 5742 ophthalmology cases (2.0%), with an increasing overall trend in hospital-based relative frequency (p < 0.001). All horses received medical treatment, and 90 (78.9%) also underwent surgery. Follow-up was available for 98 of 114 horses (86.0%): 78 (79.6%) recovered, 12 (12.2%) had persistent disease, and 8 (8.2%) underwent enucleation. Among recovered horses, median recovery time was 30 days. Exploratory analyses associated surgery with longer recovery (p < 0.001) and corneal lesion morphology with adverse outcome (p = 0.020), but treatment was clinician-selected. These findings describe EKC in one referral-hospital population but do not establish population incidence, seasonal risk, breed predisposition, or comparative treatment efficacy.

title: Plasma Carrier Proteins as Supramolecular Nanovectors for Cancer Therapy: The Trojan Horse Approach.
abstract: Conventional chemotherapeutics often suffer from poor aqueous solubility, short circulation half-lives, lack of tumor selectivity, and present dose-limiting systemic toxicity. This perspective examines the Trojan Horse Approach (THA), in which plasma carrier proteins (PCPs) are exploited as discrete, non-covalent supramolecular hosts for chemotherapeutic agents, and discusses its potential to overcome the limitations of both free drugs and conventional protein nanoparticles. Two principal strategies for assembling ex vivo drug-protein complexes are discussed: (i) molecular recognition, in which drugs occupy native ligand-binding pockets, and (ii) molecular anchoring, in which drugs are conjugated to high-affinity anchor ligands. The perspective critically assesses the current state of the art, distinguishes different levels of experimental validation, and discusses the major limitations and barriers to clinical translation. Structural, biochemical, and pharmacological evidence is examined for human serum albumin, transferrin, transthyretin, alpha-1-acid glycoprotein, alpha-fetoprotein, lactoferrin, and other plasma proteins. When appropriately designed and validated, protein-based complexes may preserve the native protein structure while conferring improved drug solubility, protection from premature metabolism, prolonged systemic circulation and enhanced tumor accumulation via combined passive and active targeting. PCPs represent a versatile and underexploited toolbox for cancer drug delivery. Expanding the repertoire of protein carriers, applying in silico rational design to guide the selection and optimization of drug-protein complexes, and exploring the use of patient-derived autologous proteins may open new opportunities for more effective and personalized therapies.

title: MicroRNA signatures of equine asthma phenotypes in serum and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid.
abstract: Equine asthma (EA) is a highly prevalent, chronic, inflammatory disease of the lower airways ranging from mild-to-moderate to severe clinical presentations. Diagnosis currently relies on bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) cytology, an invasive method associated with interobserver variability, which highlights the need for more reproducible approaches. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are small noncoding RNAs involved in gene regulation. They are stable and readily detectable in body fluids and have shown promising results as biomarkers in human asthma. The aim of this pilot study was to characterize miRNA expression profiles in BALF and serum from horses with distinct EA phenotypes to evaluate their biomarker potential and explore their putative involvement in disease pathogenesis. A total of 43 horses were included and classified as either EA (n = 32) or controls (n = 11), based on clinical examination and BALF cytology. The EA horses were further divided into three phenotypes based on BALF inflammatory cell composition: neutrophilic asthma (n = 10), mastocytic asthma (n = 15), and mixed asthma (n = 7). RNA was isolated from both serum and BALF samples and analyzed by quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) targeting 103 miRNAs linked to asthma and pulmonary inflammation in humans. Differential miRNA expression was analyzed across EA phenotypes. The most significantly differentially expressed miRNAs were used for hypothesis-generation by in silico target prediction and pathway enrichment exploratory analyses. Horses with mixed EA had significantly lower levels of eca-miR-125a-3p and eca-miR-125b-5p in BALF compared to controls. Additionally, eca-miR-146a-5p expression was significantly increased in BALF from horses with neutrophilic EA compared to mastocytic EA. For serum, none of the miRNAs showed significant differential expression within the EA phenotypes. Target and pathway enrichment analyses for eca-miR-146a-5p identified immune-relevant pathways supporting its possible involvement in inflammatory processes associated with asthma. This study identified three promising candidates, eca-miR-125a-3p, eca-miR-125b-5p, and eca-miR-146a-5p, as potential biomarkers in BALF associated with different EA phenotypes. These miRNAs are interesting candidates for further validation in an independent cohort before they can be used in diagnostics.

title: Antiviral activity of amenamevir alone and in combination with ganciclovir against equine herpesvirus 1.
abstract: Equine herpesvirus 1 (EHV-1) causes respiratory disease, abortion, and equine herpesvirus myeloencephalopathy (EHM), a neurological disorder characterized by ataxia and hindlimb paralysis. Although EHM remains a major concern in the equine industry, effective antiviral treatment options are limited. This study evaluated the antiviral activity of amenamevir, a helicase-primase complex inhibitor, against multiple EHV-1 strains using real-time cell analysis (RTCA) and quantitative PCR (qPCR), and compared its potency with those of ganciclovir, acyclovir, and penciclovir. Eight EHV-1 strains associated with different clinical manifestations and characterized by A, G, or C at position 2254 of open reading frame 30, which encodes the viral DNA polymerase, were examined. RTCA-based half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) values were calculated from inhibition rates based on the area under the normalized cell index curve. Across the eight strains, IC50 values were 0.45-2.31 μg/mL for amenamevir, 0.45-3.95 μg/mL for ganciclovir, 17.93-50.15 μg/mL for acyclovir, and 8.38-24.52 μg/mL for penciclovir. qPCR analysis, based on concentrations required to achieve a 1-log10 reduction in viral genome copy number, showed a similar overall trend. Amenamevir exhibited in vitro antiviral activity against EHV-1, with potency comparable to that of ganciclovir and greater than those of acyclovir and penciclovir. SynergyFinder analysis showed synergistic interactions between amenamevir and ganciclovir within selected concentration ranges against EHV-1 strains in both the Bliss independence and ZIP models. These findings support further investigation of amenamevir, alone and in combination with ganciclovir, as a candidate antiviral compound for the treatment of EHV-1 infection.

title: Multimodal characterization of equine synovitis: Correlation between arthroscopic, histopathological, and biomarker assessments in septic vs. aseptic cases.
abstract: Endoscopy and synovial membrane histology are complementary modalities for evaluating synovial inflammation. Cytokine involvement in non-septic arthritis is well documented but remains poorly characterized in septic synovitis. This study aimed to characterize the inflammatory cytokine profile associated with septic and non-septic synovitis and assess correlations among endoscopic, histological, and synovial fluid biomarker findings. Three groups were defined: horses undergoing elective or therapeutic endoscopy (Group 1, n=26), horses with confirmed septic synovitis (Group 2, n=25; 20 underwent endoscopic evaluation), and horses with perisynovial injuries without synovial involvement (Group 3, n=19). Synovial fluid was analysed for cell count, total protein, neutrophil percentage, and cytokine concentrations. Endoscopic and histological scores were assigned in Groups 1 and 2. Statistical analyses included non-parametric, correlation tests, and principal component analysis (PCA). Endoscopic and histological scores were significantly higher in Group 2 than in Group 1 (P=.004 and P=.006, respectively). Synovial fluid cellularity was significantly higher in Group 2 (median, 19,000 cells/µL; IQR, 11,800-81,930; P<.001). IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-10 concentrations were significantly higher in Group 2 than in Groups 1 and 3, with IL-6 reaching a median concentration of 1,416.51 (IQR, 645.49-5,225.84) in Group 2. These four cytokines contributed most strongly to group discrimination in the PCA. Combining endoscopic and histological evaluation with cytokine profiling provided a more comprehensive assessment of septic synovitis. IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-10 emerged as promising biomarkers of synovial sepsis.

title: Draft genome sequence analysis of a multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli sequence type 3602 isolated from an equine placentitis lesion in Kentucky, USA.
abstract: We report the draft genome sequence of a multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli isolate recovered from an equine placentitis lesion associated with late-term abortion. This genome expands available genomic resources for equine-associated E. coli and supports investigation of antimicrobial resistance in equine reproductive disease.

title: Bacterial isolates and antimicrobial susceptibility patterns in tracheal wash samples from horses with equine asthma in Poland.
abstract: Equine asthma (EA) is a chronic inflammatory lower-airway disease. Bacterial growth from tracheal wash (TW) may occur in samples from horses with EA, but may represent colonisation rather than active infection. This study described cultivable bacterial isolates recovered from TW samples from horses with EA in Poland and assessed their antimicrobial susceptibility patterns and association with month/season of sampling and airway neutrophil percentage. In total, 165 adult horses diagnosed with EA according to American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine-based criteria underwent endoscopy, TW sampling with a double-guarded catheter and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid cytology. The samples were cultured conventionally and their bacterial content identified with MALDI-TOF MS; bacteria were tested for antimicrobial susceptibility. Associations between culture results and categorical variables were analysed using chi-squared/Fisher-type tests with Monte Carlo simulation where appropriate; effect size was reported as Cramer's V. Culture results were positive in 117/165 horses' samples (70.9%), and bacteria were isolated from 116/165 (70.3%). The most frequently recovered bacteria were Streptococcus equi subsp. zooepidemicus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Klebsiella pneumoniae. Culture positivity was not associated with month or season of sampling, whereas analysis of bacterial genus by month suggested a modest association (χ2 = 100.72, degrees of freedom = 77, P-value = 0.036; Cramer's V = 0.305). No clear association was observed with airway neutrophil percentage. Antimicrobial susceptibility patterns varied by organism. Cultivable bacteria are frequently recovered from TW samples of horses with EA. Positive culture results should not be interpreted as evidence of bacterial infection without supporting clinical and cytological findings. Antimicrobial treatment, when clinically justified, should be guided by culture and susceptibility testing.

title: Detection of CJC-1295 in Equine Plasma by ELISA.
abstract: CJC-1295 is a peptide-based drug that stimulates the endogenous production of growth hormone (GH). Compared to other growth hormone releasing hormone (GHRH) analogues, CJC-1295 has an extended half-life due to a drug affinity complex (DAC) that chemically crosslinks the peptide to plasma proteins containing free cysteine residues. As a result, CJC-1295 behaves more like a protein doping agent than a typical peptide-based drug. Using monoclonal antibodies raised against the CJC-1295 peptide, an ELISA was developed for the detection of CJC-1295 protein conjugates in equine plasma at concentrations as low as 12.5 pg/mL. The effectiveness of the assay for controlling the illicit use of CJC-1295 was demonstrated using equine blood samples, obtained from thoroughbred racehorses, following subcutaneous administration of 10 mg of CJC-1295.

title: Pasture area increases livestock rabies risk in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil: a geospatial analysis of neurological syndrome cases (2020-2024).
abstract: Animal rabies poses a risk to livestock in Brazil due to transmission by hematophagous bats. The Brazilian sanitary surveillance system mandates rabies testing for any livestock exhibiting signs of neurological syndrome. This geospatial, retrospective, longitudinal, observational study analyzed rabies test results for 204 cattle and 56 horses presenting with neurological syndrome in Rio de Janeiro State, Brazil, from 2020 to 2024. We calculated correlations and linear models between rabies results and municipal land-use types, as well the population of herbivores. Most neurological syndrome cases and positive rabies results occurred in cattle. The final linear model for the number of neurological syndrome cases and positive rabies results incorporated pasture area, shrub area and cattle population. Pasture area was positively correlated with higher numbers (p = 0.011 and p = 0.005, respectively). Larger shrub area was associated with fewer neurological syndrome reports and fewer positive results (p = 0.009 and p = 0.010, respectively). Greater cattle population showed a negative association with neurological syndrome notifications and positive detections (p = 0.085 and p = 0.046, respectively).A higher proportion of positive rabies tests was associated with larger pasture areas (p = 0.019) and with lower equine populations (p = 0.115). These findings indicate that the lower animal diversity in pasture areas provides few alternative feeding options for Desmodus rotundus besides livestock, leading to more neurological syndrome cases and animal rabies infections. A larger shrub area offer feed alternatives other than cattle to the bats and a larger cattle population dilutes the frequency of bat meals across individuals, reducing both neurological syndrome notifications and positive rabies detections.

title: Species-specific inflammatory responses of chondrocytes: Toward evidence-based model selection in OA research.
abstract: To inform evidence-based osteoarthritis model selection, this study compares inflammatory responses of articular chondrocytes from six species (human, horse, sheep, rabbit, rat, and mouse) under standardized IL-1β and TNF-α stimulation in 2D and 3D culture. Chondrocytes were assessed for viability, proliferation, wound healing, and transcriptomic changes via RT-qPCR and 3'RNA sequencing. Marked interspecies differences were observed in morphology, proliferation, and inflammatory gene activation, with only two genes (SOD2, NFKBIA) conserved across all species. Human, horse, and rat chondrocytes shared pathways including acute phase response, deubiquitination, and class-A/1-GPCR signaling. Species-specific responses included matrix remodeling in horses, rheumatoid arthritis-related pathways in sheep, and mixed inflammatory-regenerative profiles in rats. While no species fully replicates human OA, equine and rat chondrocytes best reflect key aspects of human inflammation. These findings underscore the need for molecular criteria in model selection and advocate for human cell-based models when interspecies differences limit the translational value of animal models.

title: Bovine blood products modulate the effect of ophthalmic antibiotics against common bacterial pathogens in dogs with infectious keratitis.
abstract: Bacterial keratitis is a common condition that can result in serious complications including vision impairment and loss of the eye if not treated aggressively. Topical blood products are often utilized concurrently with topical antibiotics for their known anti-collagenolytic properties. These blood products contain albumin that could affect the antibiotic efficacy due to drug-protein binding. In this study, serum and plasma were harvested from 10 healthy bovines, utilizing fresh and frozen (1 month at -20 °C) aliquots for the experiment. Albumin and alpha-2 macroglobulin levels were quantified using species-specific ELISA kits. 30 bacterial isolates (10 Staphylococcus pseudintermedius, 10 Streptococcus canis, 10 Pseudomonas aeruginosa), isolated from canine patients with infectious keratitis were tested with blank plates as well as commercial susceptibility plates (Sensititre™ JOEYE2) to assess the minimal inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 17 different antibiotics in the absence (control) or presence of serum or plasma (fresh or frozen) from bovines (4 test groups). Mean bovine albumin levels ranged from 1.98 to 2.00 mg/ml. The median bovine alpha-2 macroglobulin levels were similar between frozen serum (4,403 ng/ml [range 3,542-5,499 ng/ml]) and frozen plasma (4,959 ng/ml [range 3,305-5,447 ng/ml]). No bacteriological susceptibility differences were noted between fresh and frozen samples for either serum or plasma. Bovine serum/plasma had direct antimicrobial effects in selected bacterial isolates (up to 49% with frozen plasma for Staphylococcus pseudintermedius). When compared with control, bovine serum/plasma increased MICs (1.33-4-fold) or decreased MICs (0.5-0.75 fold) depending on the specific antibiotic and bacterial isolate. In practice, clinicians should consider using bovine serum/plasma over other species' blood products (equine or canine) given direct antimicrobial effects, good anti-collagenolytic potential, and lesser impact on antimicrobial susceptibility to topical antibiotics. Serum and plasma can alter antibiotic efficacy (antibiotic-protein binding from high levels of albumin); therefore, serum/plasma should be applied last and spaced ≥15 min after topical antibiotics.

title: From bodyweight to biomarkers: Season-associated metabolic, endocrine and haematological shifts in breeding stallions.
abstract: Breeding stallions are subjected to sustained seasonal metabolic, endocrine, and immune demands requiring systemic energy engagement. Prospective longitudinal data in the same individuals are limited. To screen adaptive responses of breeding stallions of clinical relevance through longitudinal characterisation of temporal changes across the mating season and negative photoperiod: (i) health and nutritional status; (ii) oxidative status and immune modulation; and (iii) metabolic and endocrine biomarkers as correlates of reproductive potential. Prospective longitudinal observational cohort study. Ten clinically healthy breeding stallions (mixed breeds, age 8-22 years; bwt 496-625 kg) were assessed at P0 (start), P1 (mid-season), P2 (end of season) and P3 (negative photoperiod). Bodyweight, body condition score (BCS; Henneke 1-9) and muscle condition score (MCS; 1-5) were recorded alongside complete blood count, plasma leptin, testosterone, catalase, non-esterified fatty acids (NEFA) and beta-hydroxybutyrate (BHB). Six derived leucocyte ratios were calculated. Non-parametric repeated-measures tests were applied (Friedman/Kruskal-Wallis; Wilcoxon post hoc with Bonferroni correction). Bodyweight was stable (p = 0.86), yet pre-season NEFA were increased (P0: 0.354 mmol/L; p 13 years. Leucocytes fell from 7.59 to 0.83 × 109/L at P2 (p < 0.001), recovering at P3. Derived ratios confirmed proportional immunosuppression (NLR stable P0-P2, doubling at P3; p = 0.0004) and a 13-fold PLR rise at P2 (p < 0.001). NLR correlated with testosterone (r = -0.315; p = 0.048) and ELR with leptin (r = -0.372; p = 0.018). Intra-timepoint correlations between testosterone and WBC were consistently negative (P0: r = -0.090; P1: r = -0.202; P2: r = -0.298; P3: r = -0.559, p = 0.093). The mating season elicits subclinical metabolic adaptations and marked reversible leukopenia in clinically healthy stallions. Derived ratios demonstrate proportional immunosuppression and a leptin-eosinophil axis, supporting an integrated biomarker-based approach to preventive medicine.

title: Superior Post-Thaw Sperm Quality and Fertility of Epididymal Compared with Ejaculated Sperm in Subfertile Stallions.
abstract: Despite the benefits of seminal plasma during breeding, its value is questionable when utilizing biotechnological approaches such as artificial insemination. In addition, deleterious effects of secretions from accessory glands on sperm viability and conception rate have been reported, especially in stallions with poor semen quality. The present study aimed to compare the kinetics, structural and functional viability, and fertility parameters of spermatozoa obtained from the ejaculate and from the cauda epididymis of subfertile stallions, as well as to evaluate the differences in the electrolyte composition of the seminal plasma of animals with high versus low fertility. The kinetic parameters of the sperm samples were evaluated by computerized analysis (CASA, HTM IVOS, Hamilton Thorne Research) and the plasma membrane integrity, acrosomal integrity, sperm membrane peroxidation, DNA fragmentation, sperm capacitation, membrane phosphatidylserine translocation, and caspase activation by flow cytometry analysis. After thawing, epididymal sperm from subfertile stallions exhibited better sperm kinetics, structural and functional viability, and fertility than ejaculated sperm. Sodium concentration in seminal plasma was higher in subfertile than in fertile stallions. These findings support a potential association between the seminal environment and sperm function in subfertile stallions, although the specific contribution of seminal plasma and the components involved remain to be determined.

title: Discovery and characterization of miranthins, "Trojan horse" antibiotic modulators of bacterial composition in the oral microbiome.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
abstract: Bacteria of the human microbiota encode an abundance of natural products that likely mediate bacterial competition, local colonization patterns, and human health and disease. However, very few of these compounds have been identified and characterized to date. During our investigation of Streptococcus mitis, an important early colonizer of the oral cavity, we identified and structurally characterized a family of peptide natural products, termed miranthins herein, that contain an unusual macrocycle formed by an Asp-Cys β-carbon thioether crosslink. We determined that the most abundantly secreted miranthin is a "Trojan horse" antibiotic that enters sensitive cells via the Ami oligopeptide transporter, is hydrolyzed and activated by aminopeptidase N, and subsequently inhibits ribosomal translation to curb the growth of streptococcal competitors. The miranthins are narrow-spectrum antibiotics that could enable S. mitis to modulate community dynamics in the oral cavity, highlighting the importance of peptide natural products in interspecies competition in the microbiome.

title: An in-feed oral glucose test increases post-prandial high molecular weight adiponectin concentration in horses.
abstract: Adiponectin is a fat-derived adipocytokine that has been associated with laminitis risk in ponies. Factors that affect sampling timing for measurement of adiponectin concentration have been inadequately investigated. This study aimed to determine the effect of an oral glucose test (OGT) and fed-state on adiponectin concentration in horses and ponies. Blood samples were collected before and after an OGT in 85 horses and ponies and high molecular weight (HMW) adiponectin concentration was measured. Total adiponectin concentration was measured in a subset of 25 animals. Assays validated for use with horse plasma were used. Next, HMW adiponectin was measured before and for up to 4 hours after the consumption of three different diets in ponies: pasture (n = 16), a soyabean meal diet (n = 10) or diet with added maize and molasses (n = 5). The groups were compared with a Kruskal Wallis rank sum test, with Dunn's post-hoc test, and timepoints with a signed-rank, or Pearson's, test. The ratios were compared with a paired t-test. Stepwise rank-based regression was used to consider multiple predictors for the change in HMW adiponectin concentration during the OGT. Friedman's test was used to examine changes in concentration over time after meal consumption. Both the OGT and the diet containing maize caused a larger (P < 0.05) change in blood glucose concentration (0h to 2h) than the pasture or diet with soyabean meal. The OGT meal increased (P < 0.001) median [IQR] post-prandial HMW adiponectin concentration at the 2 h timepoint (4.02 [2.23-6.88] µg/mL), compared to the pre-test sample (2.75 [1.17-5.69] µg/mL). However, median [IQR] total adiponectin concentration did not change from the 0 h (7.78 [4.19-12.7] µg/mL) to the 2 h sample (6.48 [4.04-12.8] µg/mL). The proportion of HMW multimers in the total adiponectin concentration increased (P = 0.01) from 37% to 54% post-prandially. Pasture grazing and consumption of a soyabean or maize based meal did not result in a change in HMW adiponectin concentration over time. Blood samples for the measurement of HMW adiponectin should be taken before animals receive an in-feed OGT.

title: No armor is perfect: detecting hotspots of parasitic horse fly attacks on black caiman through 3D modeling and citizen science.
abstract: Ectoparasites often exploit anatomical weak points in their hosts, yet how their attacks are distributed across the body remains poorly understood in armored ectotherms and other organisms partly due to scarce data and the lack of spatial tools for studying parasitism on complex surfaces. This study combines citizen-science imagery with three-dimensional kernel density estimation (3D KDE) to examine 275 tabanid biting events on Melanosuchus niger, mapped onto a high-resolution 3D anatomical model. Contrary to expectations, bite intensity was unrelated to surface exposure; instead, attacks clustered in nasal and orbital regions. These findings reveal non-random, anatomy-driven parasitism and introduce a replicable spatial framework for quantifying host-parasite interactions using open-access data and morphological modeling. This complementary approach advances the ecological understanding of microhabitat selection in ectoparasites and provides new tools for exploring fine-scale interactions in elusive or logistically constrained systems.

title: Introducing a special collection on equine dentistry and sinus disease.
Effect of Different Equilibration Times in the Freezing Process on Post-Thaw Motility Parameters in Equine Spermatozoa.
abstract: Cryopreservation of stallion semen remains suboptimal, with approximately one-third of stallions producing semen that is poorly tolerant to freezing. As optimization of pre-freezing procedures may improve post-thaw sperm quality, this study evaluated the effect of different equilibration times before freezing on the post-thaw quality of stallion semen. For this purpose, 21 ejaculates were initially collected from 5 stallions and 15 were included in the final analysis after predefined exclusions. These ejaculates were separated from the seminal plasma via centrifugation in INRA 96 medium. After removal of the supernatant, each ejaculate was divided into three aliquots and equilibrated at 4°C for 2, 4, or 6 h before freezing. The pellets were mixed with INRA FREEZE solution at a concentration of 100 million spermatozoa per millilitre. Subsequently, the semen was frozen in 0.5 mL straws after being kept at the designated temperature at +4°C for either 2, 4 or 6 h post-cooling. Post-thaw sperm total motility, progressive motility and kinematic parameters were assessed by computer-assisted sperm analysis (CASA). Total motility increased with equilibration time, from 27% ± 7% after 2 h to 34% ± 10% after 4 h and 40% ± 7% after 6 h (p < 0.05). Progressive motility was significantly lower after 2 h (15% ± 6%) than after 4 h (20% ± 7%) and 6 h (22% ± 7%) of equilibration (p < 0.05), whereas no significant difference was observed between 4 and 6 h. In contrast, equilibration time did not significantly affect sperm kinematic parameters, including VAP, VSL, VCL, ALH and LIN. These findings indicate that extending the equilibration period to 6 h at 4°C before freezing improves post-thaw total and progressive sperm motility in stallions without altering the movement characteristics of surviving spermatozoa.

title: SERINC5 is the primary target of retroviral antagonists among human SERINC paralogs and requires a tri-cysteine motif for its counteraction by HIV-1 Nef.
abstract: The human transmembrane protein SERINC5 incorporates into budding HIV-1 particles and inhibits virus fusion with target cells. Although three other human SERINC paralogs display antiviral activity, their contribution to retroviral restriction and their susceptibility to viral antagonists have not been systematically compared. HIV-1 Nef, Moloney murine leukemia virus (MoMLV) glycoGag, and the equine infectious anemia virus (EIAV) S2 glycoprotein independently evolved mechanisms to counteract SERINC5. Here, we show that all human SERINC paralogs are incorporated into HIV-1 virions despite their differing antiviral activities. However, compared with the other SERINC paralogs, SERINC5 is selectively and efficiently targeted by all retroviral antagonists examined, supporting the notion that SERINC5 has exerted the strongest selective pressure on retroviral evolution. We identified a tri-cysteine motif within intracellular loop 4 (ICL4) as a critical determinant of SERINC5 antagonism by Nef. Disruption of this motif impaired Nef-mediated internalization, exclusion from virions, and full rescue of HIV-1 infectivity by diverse HIV-1 and SIV Nef alleles, but had no effect on antagonism by MoMLV glycoGag or EIAV S2, indicating that these viral proteins recognize distinct molecular features of SERINC5. Transfer of ICL4 to SERINC2 was insufficient to confer Nef sensitivity, demonstrating that the tri-cysteine motif is necessary but not sufficient for antagonism. Finally, we show that this motif is palmitoylated, suggesting that palmitoylation contributes to SERINC5 recognition by Nef. Together, these findings establish SERINC5 as the principal target of retroviral antagonists and demonstrate that its recognition by Nef depends on the broader structural context of SERINC5. The SERINC family of multipass transmembrane proteins includes host factors capable of restricting retrovirus infectivity. Among the five human paralogs, SERINC5 displays the strongest antiviral activity and is the only member efficiently targeted by all known retroviral antagonists, including HIV-1 Nef, MLV glycoGag, and the EIAV S2. This selectivity indicates that the evolutionary pressure exerted by SERINC proteins on retroviruses has been primarily driven by SERINC5 rather than by its relatives. Through structure-guided mutagenesis, we identified a tri-cysteine motif within intracellular loop 4 as a crucial determinant for SERINC5 downregulation by Nef, providing a molecular explanation for its distinctive susceptibility. These findings establish SERINC5 as the principal target of viral counteraction and suggest that its molecular features have contributed to shaping the adaptation of primate lentiviral Nef proteins to the host.

title: Host-mediated filtering and interspecific associations structure strongyle parasite communities in Sable Island horses.
abstract: Mixed-species parasite infections are common in wildlife, yet the ecological processes that structure these communities remain poorly understood. We hypothesized that host-mediated and extrinsic environmental filtering, alongside biotic interactions, act concurrently to shape parasite community composition, and that these structuring patterns would depend on parasite traits or evolutionary history. We applied nemabiome DNA metabarcoding to 3147 faecal samples from 916 feral horses with no history of anthelmintic treatment, collected over 10 years as part of a long-term individual-based study on Sable Island, Canada. Using joint species distribution models, we tested whether strongyle parasite communities were structured by host-associated factors, extrinsic environmental variables or interspecific interactions. Host factors, particularly age and individual identity, explained the greatest proportion of variation in both parasite prevalence and infection intensity, indicating strong host-mediated environmental filtering. In contrast, spatial location and year explained minimal variation, suggesting weaker effects of extrinsically mediated environmental filtering. Parasite traits such as body size and gut site preference had limited associations with species' environmental responses. Positive species associations were common, particularly among species occupying the same gut region, suggesting that strong, consistent competitive interactions were not prominently reflected in the residual covariance structure. Negative associations were less frequent but consistently involved Strongylus equinus, indicating potential context-dependent biotic interactions involving this species. By integrating species-level molecular data with hierarchical joint species models, this study quantifies patterns of host-related filtering and species co-variation within a natural parasite community and provides a framework for examining mixed infections in wild systems.

title: Heel movement and foot biomechanics in aluminium nail-on and indirect glue-on fabric cuff shoes in horses.
abstract: Heel movement is critical to shock absorption and vascular perfusion of the equine digit. Conventional horseshoeing techniques are suspected to restrict natural hoof deformation, affecting hoof biomechanics. Several studies have explored the effects of shoeing on hoof function, though many have been limited to artificial conditions, cadavers, or homogenous populations. We aimed to compare the effects of two aluminium shoeing techniques, nail-on versus indirect glue-on fabric cuff shoes, on heel movement in horses. Our objective was to determine which technique allowed greater heel movement on hard and soft footing. A controlled in vivo experimental study using a repeated-measures design. Fifteen healthy horses underwent three trials: (1) indirect glue-on fabric cuff shoes, (2) barefoot, and (3) aluminium nail-on shoes. A displacement sensor was affixed to the heels of one forelimb. Measurements were taken on hard and soft footing. Data were analysed using mixed-model ANOVA to determine differences in heel movement. Heel movement was significantly greater when barefoot (p < 0.0001). Mean heel displacement for the walk on hard ground was highest in barefoot horses (3.03 ± 0.67 mm), followed by glue-on shoes (2.23 ± 0.58 mm), and aluminium nail-on shoes (1.96 ± 0.48 mm). At the trot, mean heel movement was greatest in barefoot horses (3.29 ± 0.62 mm), followed by glue-on shoes (2.56 ± 0.55 mm), and aluminium nail-on shoes (2.12 ± 0.47 mm). The two main limitations were: (1) The lack of an absolute zero baseline measurement, preventing differentiating between heel expansion and contraction. (2) Low heel conformation in some horses prevented recordings on soft footing, reducing the statistical power. This study reinforces previous findings that shoeing restricts heel movement. Indirect glue-on shoes allow for more heel movement than nail-on shoes at the trot; both techniques limit heel movement compared to barefoot.

title: Early pregnancy after embryo transfer in artificial-cycle and cycling recipient mares and donor embryo yield across calendar-defined periods: A five-year retrospective commercial study.
abstract: Seasonal reproductive inactivity may limit year-round equine embryo transfer (ET), although artificial-cycle protocols can expand recipient availability. To compare early pregnancy after ET between artificial-cycle and cycling recipients and donor embryo yield per flush opportunity between calendar-defined pre-breeding and breeding periods. Retrospective records from a commercial ET program in Mexico (2021-2025) were analyzed. Early pregnancy was evaluated in 231 ET procedures using mixed-effects logistic regression with recipient status and year as fixed effects and recipient mare as a random intercept. Donor embryo yield was analyzed using Poisson generalized estimating equations with calendar period and year as fixed effects, donor mare as the clustering variable, and log(number of flush attempts) as an offset. Early pregnancy was 74.5% (38/51) in artificial-cycle recipients and 65.0% (117/180) in cycling recipients. Recipient status was not associated with early pregnancy (P = 0.244), whereas year was associated with the outcome (P = 0.0019). Donor data comprised 67 donor-year records, 344 flush attempts, and 250 embryos. Embryo yield was 0.667 embryos/flush during the pre-breeding period and 0.777 embryos/flush during the breeding season. The adjusted rate ratio was 0.832 (95% CI, 0.668-1.036; P = 0.100). Within the pre-breeding period, yield was 0.633 embryos/flush in 2021-2023 and 0.701 embryos/flush in 2024-2025 (rate ratio, 1.160; 95% CI, 0.896-1.502; P = 0.259). No statistically detectable difference in early pregnancy rate was observed between artificial-cycle and cycling recipients. No statistically detectable difference in donor embryo yield was observed between the calendar-defined periods after adjustment for flush opportunities.

title: Understanding Stallion Sperm Capacitation: Species-Specific Mechanisms, Cryocapacitation, and Implications for IVF.
abstract: Until recently, no repeatable protocol for equine in vitro fertilization (IVF) had been established, despite decades of trying. Recent studies have demonstrated reproducible IVF outcomes under specific experimental conditions, bringing equine IVF into a new perspective. Prolonged incubation of stallion spermatozoa in a TALP based medium supplemented with penicillamine, hypotaurine and epinephrine (PHE) appears to be important factors of protocols that support sperm capacitation and markedly improved IVF outcomes. The sperm capacitation procedure has now been applied successfully using both fresh and frozen-thawed stallion semen, with the latter requiring a shorter pre-incubation period. Here, we review the molecular, structural, and metabolic processes that drive capacitation in stallion spermatozoa, with comparisons to better-characterized mechanisms in other mammals, focusing on changes in sperm membrane composition, energy metabolism, cytoplasmic content, and on the influences of seminal plasma and the female reproductive tract. Because the newly developed IVF protocol appears to be shorter with frozen-thawed semen, special attention is given to capacitation-like changes triggered by cryopreservation, and their consequences for sperm function and fertilizing capacity. Importantly, although successful fertilization can be achieved under these conditions, this does not constitute direct evidence that the molecular mechanisms governing stallion sperm capacitation have been fully elucidated. Rather, these protocols provide a robust experimental platform for investigating these mechanisms in the horse.

title: The Effect of Training Exercise on Cartilage Zonal Composition and Structure at Two Differently Loaded Sites in the Juvenile Equine Metacarpophalangeal Joint.
abstract: BackgroundThe aim of this study was to investigate the depth related spatial distribution of biochemical and structural components in articular cartilage at different topographical sites experiencing different loading within the juvenile equine metacarpophalangeal joint in two groups of foals subjected to different exercise conditions.MethodsSixteen Warmblood foals were included in the study and were randomly assigned into 1 of 2 exercise groups (box rest and box rest plus training) during the first 5 months of life and subsequently euthanized. Osteochondral plugs were harvested from two sites which have previously been shown to experience different load levels and sectioned into 100 μm thick slices. Cartilage slices were analysed for glycosaminoglycan, DNA, and total collagen content, as well as content of hydroxylysine residues (HYL) in collagen and the collagen cross-link Hydroxylysylpyridinoline (HP). Collagen fibril architecture (Orientation Angle and Parallelism Index) was determined using quantitative polarized light microscopy.ResultsThe constantly loaded site 2 exhibited higher glycosaminoglycan (GAG) and HP content with HYL higher in the superficial and middle layers of the trained group, while the intermittently peak loaded site 1 showed greater collagen accumulation in deeper layers but lower cross-link density. Structural analyses (Oa and PI) confirmed that collagen fibril orientation and alignment adapt regionally, with training enhancing fibril organization in superficial zones.ConclusionThis study illustrates that mechanical loading is a key driver of functional adaptation, resulting in distinct zonal and topographical differences in the biochemical and structural composition of equine cartilage at 5 months.

title: Effects of Incorporating Horses into Occupational Therapy on Adrenocortical and Sympathetic Nervous System Reactivity and Regulation in Autistic Children: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
journal: Journal of autism and developmental disorders
abstract: The study prospectively investigated adrenocortical and autonomic nervous system reactivity and regulation as autistic children participated in a randomized controlled trial of occupational therapy in an equine environment (OT-Equine). Autistic children (n = 72, ages 6-11 yrs) were randomly assigned for 10 weeks to OT-Equine or clinic-based occupational therapy (OT-Clinic). Saliva samples (later assayed for cortisol and alpha-amylase, [sAA]) were collected before (pre-session), during (within-session), immediately after (post-session), and 20-minutes after (post-session + 20) each 1-hour weekly session. Data were analyzed with a generalized linear mixed-effects model. Across the 10 sessions, pre-session sAA significantly increased (exp(b) = 1.02 per week, p 0.05). Within session, however, cortisol concentrations decreased from pre- to post- and post-session + 20, with greater reductions among OT-Equine participants (exp(b) = 0.77; p < 0.01). Changes in cortisol were associated with improved treatment outcomes. The pattern of reactivity and recovery in sAA suggests that children experienced autonomic/sympathetic arousal in response to therapy sessions, perhaps associated with excitement and positive affect. Moreover, stable pre-session cortisol concentrations across sessions for both groups, and declining cortisol concentrations within sessions for the OT-Equine group, suggests OT-Equine participants also held subjective experiences characterized by familiarity and low levels of distress. Taken together, findings suggest the integration of horses into occupational therapy for autistic children creates an exciting positive therapeutic environment, associated with improved treatment outcomes. The study was registered as a clinical trial at clinicaltrials.gov (NCT05846932, registered April 26, 2023).

title: Distribution of Losses Among Horse Race Bettors: An Analysis of Account-Based Player Tracking Data.
abstract: Previous research on gambling loss patterns has mainly relied on self-reported data, which has some inherent biases (e.g., low accuracy). While some studies are based on large samples of horse bettors, few have examined how losses are distributed among them. The aim of this exploratory study was to examine the concentration of losses among gamblers playing horse betting games. Norsk Rikstoto, the Norwegian horse betting monopoly, provided account-based gambling data for all customers who bet with them between 2021 and 2023, covering 13 horse betting formats. To describe the shape of the loss distribution for each format, we calculated the mean-to-median loss ratio, the Gini coefficient, and the shares of total losses attributable to the top 1%, 5%, 10%, and 20% of bettors. Across all 13 betting formats combined, the mean-to-median loss ratio was 7.06 (min: 4.88, max: 11.53) and the Gini coefficient was 0.81 (min: 0.77, max: 0.87). Overall, the top 1% of bettors accounted for almost one-quarter of total losses (24.7%), while the top 20% accounted for 86.0%. This imbalance was most pronounced for single-race games (top 1%: 26.2-39.5%; top 20%: 87.3-91.5%) compared with the multi-race V-games (top 1%: 19.9-23.9%; top 20%: 81.0-87.5%). In summary, losses in horse betting are heavily concentrated among a relatively small share of bettors. The degree of inequality differs across game types, suggesting that product characteristics may play a role in shaping who loses and by how much.

title: Molnupiravir, first small molecule therapeutic to demonstrate therapeutic efficacy against Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus in the cynomolgus macaque model.
abstract: Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV) is an emergent arbovirus of major epidemic concern. Associated with periodic outbreaks in Central and South America, VEEV has a high morbidity rate in humans due to a 1:1 clinical-to-subclinical ratio and can cause neurological disease in up to 14% of cases. Concerningly, no FDA-approved vaccines or therapeutics for VEEV exist. Molnupiravir, an isopropyl ester prodrug of β-D-N4-hydroxycytidine, has previously showcased notable antiviral activity against VEEV in vitro and in rodents. While molnupiravir emergency use authorization has been granted for SARS-CoV-2, drug efficacy against VEEV in a translational model of human disease has yet to be investigated. We therefore performed the first study examining molnupiravir efficacy against VEEV in cynomolgus macaques, a non-lethal animal model known to reiterate clinical hallmarks of VEEV human disease. Animals treated twice-daily with 150 mg/kg molnupiravir approximately 8 h post-VEEV exposure demonstrated improved human-relevant clinical parameters, including reduced viremia, febrile illness, and lymphopenia, as well as diminished histopathological evidence of encephalitis and cerebral RNA persistence. We additionally showcased that the calculated human equivalent dose of molnupiravir (97 mg/kg BID) was insufficient in decreasing viremia or improving clinical parameters.
